Search for the optimal composition (Goldilocks zone)

Source: R/optimal_composition.R
optimal_composition.Rd

Finds the compositions with the best predicted outcome for one comp_iv() fit, or one fit per outcome, among candidates on a grid in closure units (by default every 10 minutes of a 1,440-minute day) inside a feasible region of the sample's compositions. Each outcome's zone holds the candidates whose prediction ranks in its best 1 - zone share or meets a threshold, and the closed geometric mean of the zones' intersection is the optimal composition. The search method, its arguments and its defaults may change in a later release.

Usage

optimal_composition(
  object,
  direction = "max",
  zone = 0.95,
  region = "box",
  sd = 3,
  coverage = NULL,
  spacing = NULL,
  threshold = NULL,
  widen = FALSE,
  type = c("relative", "absolute"),
  category = NULL,
  at = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  from = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95
)

# S3 method for class 'optimal_comp'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'optimal_comp'
plot(x, outcome = NULL, level = NULL, resolution = 40L, smooth = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

A comp_iv() fit, or a list of them, one per outcome, on the same parts (in the same order) and total. A list is named by outcome; an unnamed one takes each fit's outcome variable, the left-hand side of its model formula. The region is estimated from the first fit's composition.

direction

"max" (default) when a higher predicted outcome is better, "min" when a lower one is. Give one value, or one per outcome. On a Cox fit ("cox", "coxme"), "max" favours the highest hazard, and a search for the lowest risk uses "min". On an ordinal fit ("clm", "clmm"), the cumulative logit \(P(Y \le j) = \mathrm{logit}^{-1}(\theta_j - \eta)\) moves probability to the higher outcome categories as the latent predictor \(\eta\) rises. "max" therefore favours the higher categories. On a multinomial fit, "max" favours the category level over the reference level.

zone

The rank a candidate needs to be in an outcome's zone, a number in (0, 1); the default 0.95 keeps the best 5%.

region

The feasible region. "box" (default) sets per-part limits (Dumuid et al. 2021; Brakenridge et al. 2024). "ellipsoid" is the chi-square ellipsoid in ILR coordinates of Mellow et al. (2026). "observed" takes the sample's own compositions (Lund Rasmussen et al. 2023; Vindiš et al. 2025). A data frame gives the compositions directly, one column per part on the closure scale; every row must be positive and sum to the fit's total.

sd

For "box": a positive number of standard deviations, default 3. Each part is limited to its mean \(\pm\) sd standard deviations on the closure scale, never beyond the part's observed range. Passing sd with another region, or with coverage, is an error, and sd = NULL needs coverage.

coverage

For "box", NULL (default) uses sd. Otherwise the box takes percentile limits in place of sd: either the quantiles c(lo, hi) or one share for the central quantiles c((1 - coverage) / 2, (1 + coverage) / 2). For "ellipsoid", the chi-square level of its boundary, a share in (0, 1), default 0.80; the printed result also gives the share of the sample inside. coverage is ignored, with a message, for the other regions.

spacing

For "box" and "ellipsoid": the grid step, a positive number of closure units. NULL (default) uses 1/144 of the closure declared in declare_composition(), 10 minutes of a 1,440-minute day. A finer grid holds more candidates, and the search stops when more than 1,000,000 lie inside the region, or more than 5,000,000 on the grid before the region is applied. The number of candidates grows steeply with the number of parts. With five or more parts the default search takes about a minute, and a coarser grid (e.g., 1/72 of the closure) shortens it.

threshold

NULL (default), or a named list with one entry per outcome ruled by a value instead of zone. An entry is one number (a cut-off, met at or above it for "max" and at or below it for "min") or two (an inclusive band; e.g., list(zbmi = c(-1, 1))). The value is on the type scale. For "relative", it is the effect versus from: a ratio, and so positive, on a ratio scale such as an odds or hazard ratio, and otherwise a difference. For "absolute", it is the predicted response.

widen

FALSE (default) keeps every zone at zone. TRUE lowers zone in steps of 0.05 for the outcomes it rules, when their zones share no candidate, until they do. It never goes below 0.5 (the Intersection item of Details). With by, each level is widened on its own.

type

"relative" (default) values each candidate by its effect versus from on the fit's effect scale, the measure predict_realloc() reports (e.g., an odds ratio, a hazard ratio or a mean difference). "absolute" values it by the predicted response, which the survival, ordinal and multinomial engines do not provide. The zone ruled by zone is the same under both. threshold, the zone limits, the estimate at the centre and plot() follow the scale.

category

For a multinomial ("mblogit") fit, the non-reference outcome level whose log-odds against the reference level is searched: required for such a fit, and refused when no fit is multinomial. NULL (default).

at

Optional named list of covariate values held in every prediction, as in predict_realloc().

by

Optional name of a factor covariate of every fit. The search then has one region and one zone per level, with the level held in its predictions. Defaults to a factor moderator not pinned by at, as in predict_realloc(), and every fit must resolve to the same by.

from

The composition the gain is measured from, and with it every value of a type = "relative" search. NULL (default) uses each fit's reference composition, stored by comp_iv(): the closed geometric mean of the composition the fit was given. Every level of by is measured from it. Otherwise, give a named numeric vector with one positive value per part, re-closed to the closure declared in declare_composition(). When the zone centre equals from, the gain is the reference value (0, or 1 on a ratio scale) with no test.

conf_level

Confidence level of the intervals, default 0.95.

x

An optimal_comp object.

...

Unused by print(), present for S3 consistency. plot() takes no further arguments, and one given there is an error.

outcome

The outcome whose surface is drawn; NULL (default) for the first.

level

For a search with by, the level whose zone is drawn; NULL (default) for the first. Not used without by.

resolution

For plot(), the steps along each edge of a panel's simplex, as in plot.comp_iv() (default 40).

smooth

NULL (default) draws the computed cells as tiles for a fit linear in the composition and a quadratic surface through them for any other fit; TRUE or FALSE draws the smooth or the tiles for any fit, as in plot.comp_iv(). A panel whose smooth cannot be fitted is drawn as tiles, with a warning.

Value

An optimal_comp object, a list with elements:

candidates

A tibble with one row per candidate inside the region, holding the parts on the closure scale, the ILR coordinates (ilr1, ilr2, ...), mahalanobis (the distance for the ellipsoid, else NA) and the by column. Per outcome follow estimate_<outcome>, rank_<outcome> and in_zone_<outcome>, then the overall in_zone. estimate_<outcome> is on the link scale: the prediction, or for type = "relative" its difference from the prediction at from.

zones

A tibble with one row per outcome and one "overall" row (per by level). Its columns are rule ("quantile" or "threshold"), threshold_low, threshold_high, n, per part centre_<part>, min_<part>, max_<part> and best_<part>, then on_boundary, and q_overlap on the overall row. The two thresholds are the limits the zone's values meet, on the type scale (the effect versus from, or the predicted response). best_<part> is the best-ranked candidate; for the overall zone, it is the candidate whose lowest rank across outcomes is highest.

optimum

A tibble with one row per outcome (per by level). Its columns are the parts of the centre evaluated, centre_of ("overall", or "outcome" when the zones do not overlap), and estimate, conf.low and conf.high at that centre on the type scale. Under "relative" the estimate is the effect versus from and equals the gain; under "absolute" it is the predicted response. The gain from from follows on the fit's effect scale (gain, gain.low, gain.high, p.value), then the from parts as from_<part>.

fits

The fits, named by outcome, which plot() draws.

Settings

direction, zone (as given), threshold, widen, type, category, region, the coverage, sd and spacing used (NULL where they do not apply), n_candidates (per level) and zone_used (per level, the zone searched, which is zone or the step widen reached). It also holds parts, labels, units, total, outcomes, linear (per outcome, TRUE for a fit with no curvature term), measures (the gain's effect label per outcome), by, at and conf_level. region holds its name and, per level, its estimated parameters. For the ellipsoid these include the limit r2 on the squared distance and share, the share of the level's sample inside. For the box they are the per-part limits lo and hi and the flags lo_clipped and hi_clipped, TRUE where a limit was cut to the part's observed minimum or maximum; print() reports those.

Details

Every prediction comes from emmeans, on the reference grid predict_realloc() uses. With type = "relative" (default), a candidate's value is its contrast with from (by default the reference composition) on the fit's effect scale, as for a predict_realloc() reallocation, so every engine of comp_iv() can be searched. With type = "absolute", the value is the predicted response.

The search runs in this order.

  1. Region. The feasible region is estimated from the sample's compositions, per level of by. The default "box" limits every part, on the closure scale, to its mean \(\pm\) sd standard deviations, 3 by default (Dumuid et al. 2021). With coverage, the limits are a pair of the part's quantiles instead (Brakenridge et al. 2024 use the 1st and 99th percentiles). No limit extends beyond the part's observed range. The "ellipsoid" region holds the compositions whose squared Mahalanobis distance from the mean of the pivot isometric log-ratio (ILR) coordinates is at most the coverage quantile of the chi-square distribution on \(D - 1\) degrees of freedom (Mellow et al. 2026). That distance is \((z - \bar z)^\top S^{-1} (z - \bar z)\), with \(S\) the sample covariance. "observed" takes the sample's own compositions as the candidates (Lund Rasmussen et al. 2023), and a data frame takes the compositions it holds.

  2. Candidates. For "box" and "ellipsoid", the candidates are the compositions inside the region whose first D - 1 parts are positive multiples of spacing, the last part being the remainder of the closure declared in declare_composition(). The default spacing is 1/144 of that closure, the 10-minute grid of Dumuid et al. (2021) on a 1,440-minute day; Mellow et al. (2026) use 5 minutes. The search stops with an error when more than 1,000,000 candidates lie inside the region, or when the grid holds more than 5,000,000 compositions before the region is applied.

  3. Prediction. Each outcome is predicted at every candidate on the fit's link scale. For type = "relative", each prediction is contrasted there with the prediction at from. As in predict_realloc(), factor covariates that do not interact with the composition are averaged with equal weight, and numeric ones are held at their mean. Each emmeans reference grid holds many candidates, so a search over tens of thousands of them takes a few seconds.

  4. Zone. A candidate's rank is the share of candidates whose link-scale prediction is no better than its own (ties averaged), so it is the same for both values of type. An outcome's zone holds the candidates whose rank is at least zone. For an outcome named in threshold, a candidate is in the zone when its value on the type scale (the effect versus from, or the predicted response) meets the cut-off or lies in the band (Vindiš et al. 2025). In this package, the rule "healthy below the 85th percentile" of Lund Rasmussen et al. (2023) is direction = "min", zone = 0.15, which keeps 85% of the candidates.

  5. Intersection. The overall zone holds the candidates in every outcome's zone (Dumuid et al. 2021; Duncan et al. 2024). When the zones do not overlap, q_overlap gives the largest zone at which they would share a candidate, and the intersection stays empty unless widen = TRUE. Widening lowers zone for every outcome it rules, together, in steps of 0.05 (zone - 0.05, zone - 0.10, ...) until the zones share a candidate, as in Dumuid et al. (2021) and Brakenridge et al. (2024). It stops at the first such step and never goes below 0.5, the best 50% of each outcome. A threshold is never changed. The result is that of a search at the level reached, which zone_used reports. A widened zone may not improve every outcome, and each outcome's gain and its interval show whether it does.

  6. Centre. Each zone is summarized by its closed geometric mean (the inverse ILR of its mean coordinates), its per-part range and its best-ranked candidate.

  7. Gain. Each outcome is predicted at the overall zone centre (at its own centre when the zones do not overlap) and contrasted with from, as one predict_realloc() contrast. For type = "relative", this gain is also the value reported at the centre.

A predicted outcome linear in the ILR coordinates has no interior optimum, and its zone lies on the edge of the region. A fit with no curvature term (squares, products, poly(), ns(), bs()) is still searched, with one message stating that the fit is linear in the composition. The zone of a curved fit also lies on the boundary when its stationary point is outside the region.

A zone's on_boundary value is the share of its candidates in the outer shell of the region. On the ellipsoid, that shell holds the candidates whose squared Mahalanobis distance is above 0.9 of the limit; on the box, those with a part within one spacing of a limit.

The confidence intervals of the prediction at the centre and of the gain are conditional on the centre, and the location of the zone itself has no interval.

The box, the ellipsoid and the grid do not depend on the order of the parts when spacing divides the total, as the default does.

A covariate that interacts with the composition must be pinned with at or split with by; otherwise the call aborts and names it. A factor moderator is split by default, as in predict_realloc(). With by, each level has its own region, estimated from its own rows, and its own zone. On a fit built with include_total = TRUE, every prediction holds t_total at the fit's total_ref.

type = "absolute" is refused for the engines without an absolute prediction ("cox", "coxme", "clm", "clmm" and "mblogit"; see comp_iv()). A multinomial ("mblogit") fit is searched on the log-odds of the outcome level named by category against the reference level, so each category has its own ranking and zone.

Functions

  • print(optimal_comp): Prints a text report in sections. The report gives the search's settings, each part's region limits, each zone's centre and per-part range, and the gain from from to the zone centre. The limits are the box's, or the candidates' range for another region, and a mark shows a box limit that is the part's observed minimum or maximum. With by, the limits, zones and gain are given for each level. A widened search states how far its zones were widened, and type = "absolute" adds the predicted outcome at each zone centre.

  • plot(optimal_comp): Ternary panels (choose(D, 3)) of one outcome's surface on the search's type scale (the effect versus from, or the predicted response), drawn for every engine. An ordinal fit's surface is its cumulative odds ratio versus from, and a multinomial fit's is the relative risk ratio of the searched category. Each panel is a slice through the zone centre (the overall one, or the outcome's own when the zones do not overlap). The surface is drawn as plot.comp_iv() draws one, on the cells inside the search's region. For the box and the ellipsoid these are the cells the region itself holds (on the parameters of the level drawn); otherwise they are the cells within the candidates' per-part range. The surface holds the search's at values and, for a search with by, the level drawn. The convex hull of the computed cells in the outcome's zone is outlined in red, and the centre is marked. A panel with fewer than three computed cells in the zone has no outline, and a higher resolution computes more cells. A panel carries no caption: the zone centre, the held covariates and the region's limits are in print(). Returns the plot object (one plot, or a list named by triplet), drawn as a side effect. An argument the method does not take is an error.

See also

comp_iv() to fit the models this consumes; predict_realloc() for a directed reallocation between named parts.

Other reallocation and prediction: plot_realloc(), predict_realloc(), summary.realloc()

Examples

# \donttest{
cd <- declare_composition(timeuse, c("MVPA", "LPA", "SB", "SPT"),
                          closure = 1440, units = "min/day")
quad <- comp_iv(cd, formula = zbmi ~ ilr()^2 + I(ilr()^2) + sex,
                model = "lm")
# The per-part box of the mean +/- 3 standard deviations, on a 10-minute grid
opt <- optimal_composition(quad, direction = "min")
opt
#> <optimal_comp> Goldilocks-zone search: zbmi
#> 
#> Search
#>   Parts       MVPA, LPA, SB, SPT (total = 1440 min/day)
#>   Region      per-part box of the mean +/- 3 SD
#>   Grid        multiples of 10 min/day; 36,611 candidates
#>   Scale       Mean difference versus the reference day
#>   Zone rule   best 5% of predictions, lower is better
#> 
#> Region limits (min/day)
#>           lower     upper
#>   MVPA      0.1*    180.0
#>   LPA      51.8*    503.3
#>   SB      315.6*   1013.4
#>   SPT     239.9*    809.4
#>   * the part's observed minimum
#> 
#> Zone for zbmi: 1,831 compositions (centre [min; max])
#>   MVPA   125.2  [ 30.0; 170.0]
#>   LPA    267.2  [110.0; 480.0]
#>   SB     353.9  [320.0; 410.0]
#>   SPT    693.6  [470.0; 800.0]
#> 
#> Gain from the reference day to the zone centre (95% CI)
#>   zbmi   Mean difference   -2.54  [-3.2; -1.88]  p = 5.44e-13

# Two outcomes, their zones intersected
risk <- comp_iv(cd, "obesity", model = "glm", family = "binomial")
optimal_composition(list(zbmi = quad, obesity = risk), direction = "min")
#> "obesity" is linear in the composition, so its best predicted outcome lies on
#> the edge of the region.
#> ℹ The zone then marks where the region ends; see on_boundary.
#> ℹ A curved surface can hold an interior optimum: refit with `curvature = TRUE`
#>   (or `ilr()^2 + I(ilr()^2)` in a formula).

#>               day

#>   SPT    693.6  [470.0; 800.0]

#> Zone for obesity: 1,831 compositions (centre [min; max])
#>   MVPA   151.2  [ 90.0; 170.0]

# A box from the 1st to the 99th percentile of each part, on a 20-minute grid
optimal_composition(quad, direction = "min", coverage = c(0.01, 0.99),
                    spacing = 20)

cox <- comp_iv(cd, formula = survival::Surv(time, event) ~ ilr()^2 +
                 I(ilr()^2) + sex, model = "cox")
optimal_composition(list(onset = cox), direction = "min")
